checks.name: required_audit_coverage
checks.detail: report covers all 38 Required Audit items with substantive aligned answers
required_audit_items: Was the current `decision_packet.md` treated as the only execution authority and `task_packet.json` as background only?
Did decision metadata remain valid, approved, on `engineering_branch`, and aligned with active `reverse-agent-iteration@v2`?
Were startup commands recorded before project gates?
Was startup-snapshot recorded before substantive gate/test execution?
Did Codex inspect existing pipeline, harness, job, runner, runner contract, and project gate code before implementing user-solve code?
Did implementation avoid duplicating existing pipeline, solver, harness, command-plan, execution-log, job, and AgentRunner capabilities?
Were changes limited to the allowed source/test/documentation/generated artifact paths?
Were forbidden files not modified?
Was `UserSolveResult` implemented with stable JSON/dict serialization?
Were user statuses restricted to an explicit enum including `uploaded`, `fast_analyzing`, `candidate_found`, `validating`, `verified`, `deep_analysis_running`, `failed`, and `blocked`?
Were validation statuses restricted to an explicit enum including `not_started`, `pending`, `passed`, `failed`, and `unavailable`?
Were evidence statuses restricted to an explicit enum including `none`, `partial`, `building`, `complete`, and `failed`?
Does `verified` require passed validation and a usable answer or candidate?
Does `candidate_found` allow validation to remain pending?
Does default user-visible serialization hide internal engineering paths and developer trace references?
Is there an explicit developer/debug serialization path that can retain trace references for engineering use without becoming the default user output?
Was `UserSolveStateMachine` implemented with allowed transitions and rejection of invalid transitions?
Does `blocked` require a clear reason/message?
Was `EvidenceQualityMapper` implemented to translate engineering missing_evidence into user-facing status/message without exposing raw internal files?
Does missing targeted decompile/static evidence map to `deep_analysis_running` or equivalent non-terminal user status rather than immediate user failure?
Was `FastSolveWrapper` implemented as a safe adapter over in-memory or pipeline-like result data without executing samples/tools?
Does the wrapper convert a high-confidence candidate into `candidate_found` with pending validation when validation evidence is absent?
Does the wrapper convert passed validation into `verified` only when validation evidence supports it?
Does the wrapper return a clear `failed` or no-candidate result when no candidate exists?
Does the wrapper return `blocked` with reason when the input indicates tool/environment/policy blocking?
Did tests cover invalid verified-without-validation cases?
Did tests cover candidate-before-validation behavior?
Did tests cover user-visible redaction of `project_state`, `decision_packet`, `command_plan`, `artifact_index`, `negative_results`, `codex_execution_report`, and `pytest_result` references?
Did tests cover state machine valid and invalid transitions?
Did tests cover evidence-quality mapping from missing engineering evidence to user-facing fallback status?
Did tests cover the fast wrapper candidate/verified/no-candidate/blocked branches?
Was a current gate artifact generated for the user-solve layer foundation?
Did final-check pass with current decision/report/round IDs?
Did `pytest_result.txt` match `tests_ran` in the report?
Did command-plan authorize all executed commands and omit no executed commands?
Did run-closeout pass and archive the corrected reports if command-plan authorized closeout?
Did the round avoid Web/API, DB/queue/scheduler, remote runner, GitHub Actions dispatch/polling, IDA/Ghidra/OllyDbg, IDA MCP, runtime probe, dynamic debugging, and concrete reverse solving?
Did the final report avoid claiming solved/static_verified/runtime_validated/audit_verified for any sample?
